Description
The Russian 10 Ruble gold coin is a historic and highly collectible coin originating from the Russian Empire and later Soviet-era issues. Most commonly associated with the reign of Tsar Nicholas II (1898–1911), this coin is valued both for its gold content and its rich historical significance.
Struck in high-quality gold, the 10 Rubles coin remains popular among investors and numismatists due to its classic design, durability, and intrinsic bullion value
Design Features
Obverse:
The obverse typically features a portrait of Tsar Nicholas II, surrounded by Cyrillic inscriptions identifying him as Emperor and Autocrat of All Russia.
Reverse:
The reverse displays the imperial double-headed eagle, a symbol of the Russian Empire, along with the denomination “10 РУБЛЕЙ” and the year of minting.
Each Russian 10 Rubles gold coin contains approximately
7.74 grams of pure gold
, making it equivalent to about
0.25 troy ounces
of gold.
The coin is composed of a
90% gold and 10% copper alloy
, which enhances its durability and gives it a slightly reddish tone compared to pure gold coins.
Edge:
The edge inscription indicates the gold purity and weight in traditional Russian units, along with mint master initials

Each 10 Ruble Gold Coin in this product listing is available to you in circulated condition. Coins in circulated conditions can show a range of flaws as a result of use in circulation. These types of flaws typically include wear on the designs and inscriptions, scratches, scuffs, and other visual detractions.
Investment & Collectability
Today, the Russian 10 Rubles gold coin is widely traded as both:
A
bullion investment coin
due to its gold content
A
numismatic collectible
with historical value
Its relatively small size, recognizable design, and standardized gold content make it a popular choice among collectors and investors worldwide.
